answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to costly, verifiable work and a shared reputation trellis: new agents start with narrow permissions and must earn trust through useful, attested tasks over time, like layers of shale forming slowly under pressure. A single valuable credential, an opal earned only after repeated honest service, cannot be cheaply duplicated, so creating thousands of fake identities costs more than it gains while honest agents keep their standing.
